features.feature_value: Cursing/vulgar language led to banning/removing posts.
features.evidence_span: "Foul and cursing language prompted me to ban those posts."
features.rationale: The participant explicitly links foul/cursing language to their removal decision.

features.feature_value: Wanted fairness for free speech, but profanity/threats pushed them toward removing posts.
features.evidence_span: "profanity or threats would nudge me towards removing posts."
features.rationale: They provide a stated threshold/criterion: profanity or threats increase likelihood of removal.

features.feature_value: Vulgar language signaled the author had nothing of value; kept other balanced pairs.
features.evidence_span: "It a pair of posts had vulgar language, it simply showed that whoever made those posts really had nothing of value to contribute."
features.rationale: They interpret vulgarity as indicating low substantive value, affecting keep/remove.

features.feature_value: Err on side of allowing speech, but removed when statements didn’t welcome open communication.
features.evidence_span: "I tried to err on the side of allowing speech." / "none of the statements welcomed open communication."
features.rationale: They describe both a default (allow) and a specific discursive criterion for removal.

features.feature_value: Strong opposition to moderation; views moderation as silencing opposition; only very bad cases would justify removal.
features.evidence_span: "I can't imagine why any speech would be moderated?" / "That defeats the entire point of discourse and freedom of speech."
features.rationale: Their reasoning is grounded in a strong normative stance against moderation.

features.feature_value: Kept posts that were good-faith ideology discussion; removed content driving hate or nonsensical talk.
features.evidence_span: "actual ideology discussion based in good faith" / "Anything that was blatantly and specifically driving hate or brainless nonsense got the boot."
features.rationale: They articulate explicit content-based criteria tied to keep vs remove.

features.feature_value: Mostly allowed everything under free speech/felt neutral, removing only for an indirect sexual reference.
features.evidence_span: "I only removed one post as it seemed to make an indirect sexual reference." / "Aside from that, I allowed all other posts"
features.rationale: They state a near-default keep policy with one specific exception.

features.feature_value: If both were aggressive/out of order, they opposed both; if one had a good point, they approved both based on the correct one.
features.evidence_span: "If it was aggressive or out of order on both sides I opposed both" / "it was worth approving both for that correct one."
features.rationale: They explain how they compared paired posts and sometimes kept both depending on which side contained the correct point.
